rationale: C14 is a close drafting template for the child memorandum: both identify a congressional investigative committee, express the President's desire that the Executive branch cooperate, and request cooperation from all departments and agencies subject to preserving their ordinary work and duties. The child adapts this same structure and much of its language to Chairman Chelf's House subcommittee. C25 is also closely connected to the child's immediate factual setting and likely contributed the limiting formulation, but its operative purpose is the opposite—directing agencies to decline a prior sweeping request. C12 shares the agency-cooperation memorandum form but is less distinctive and concerns a presidential commission rather than a congressional inquiry.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It is my desire that the Executive branch of the Government cooperate with the committee
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is my desire that the Executive branch of the Government cooperate with the Committee to the fullest possible extent.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive, nearly verbatim statement of presidential policy toward cooperation with a congressional investigative committee.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I now request that all departments and agencies ... cooperate with Chairman Frank L. Chelf and his subcommittee
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I therefore request that all departments and agencies give Chairman Kefauver and his committee the fullest cooperation and assistance
shared_material.explanation: The same operative request is adapted by substituting the chairman and committee.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to the fullest extent consistent with the proper performance of their work and duties
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the fullest cooperation and assistance consistent with the orderly performance of the work and duties of the departments and agencies
shared_material.explanation: Closely parallel limitation preserving the agencies' ability to perform their normal duties.
